reasons: The lake record is verified for Berghuis v. Thompkins, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 2010-06-01, year 2010.
The asserted empty official citation, vendor-neutral cite 2010 U.S. LEXIS 4379, and listed parallel cites match the lake citation fields.

defect.evidence_quote: In sum, a suspect who has received and understood the Miranda warnings, and has not invoked his Miranda rights, waives the right to remain silent by making an uncoerced statement to the police.
defect.problem: The holding is supportable in substance but the frontmatter text trails off after 'a suspect who answers questions…' and, if read broadly, omits the required conditions for implied waiver: Miranda warnings received and understood, no invocation, and an uncoerced statement.
defect.proposed_fix: Replace the holding with: The right to remain silent must be invoked unambiguously; silence alone does not invoke it; a suspect who has received and understood Miranda warnings, has not invoked Miranda rights, and makes an uncoerced statement waives the right to remain silent.

reasons: The opinion supports the unambiguous-invocation rule and says Thompkins did not invoke the right because he did not say he wanted to remain silent or did not want to talk with police.
The opinion also limits implied waiver to an uncoerced statement after Miranda warnings were received and understood, where the suspect has not invoked Miranda rights.
residual_risks: The current ellipsis makes the holding field less reliable for downstream extraction.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: State the full waiver conditions instead of ending with an ellipsis.

reasons: The opinion says the dispute centers on the suspect's response or nonresponse after Miranda warnings.
The decision directly addresses both invocation of the right to remain silent and implied waiver, supporting placement on Miranda Waiver and Invocation as a key anchor.
residual_risks: The exact editorial label Key — Anchor is not separately encoded in the lake record, but it is supported by the opinion's central holding.
